title: audit(#2657 prerequisite): refresh the two-repo metadata-type coverage matrix — registered types vs authorable schemas vs Studio pillars
body:
Prerequisite of #2657 (maintainer 2026-08-07, 「按建议」): #2657 stays **off** the v17 board; its next actionable step is this audit, whose output is the input for the maintainer's one-shot appetite ruling (ADR-0088 admission + ordering, bundled with the Studio appetite question in #3257). Likely a v18-train program — this card only measures.

## Why the existing matrix cannot be used

#2657's coverage matrix predates several structural changes measured during the 2026-08-07 release-board audit: `api` was promoted via #5312, `role`/`profile`/`validation` were retired, and the Studio pillar set has moved. Deciding admission/ordering off the stale matrix would misroute a multi-week program.

## Ask (read-only audit, both repos)

1. Enumerate the CURRENT registered metadata types (`DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` + schema entries in `packages/spec`) on objectstack `origin/main`.
2. For each promotion candidate #2657 names (webhooks, connectors, portals, sharingRules) and any additional drifted candidates found: record — registered? authorable zod schema exists? REST/meta routes? Studio pillar in objectui (which surface, how complete)? real consumers (grep, per Operational-note-6 discipline: quoted exact names, declaration-site over mention).
3. Produce the refreshed matrix as a table: type × {registry, schema, routes, Studio, consumers, ADR-0088 admission blockers}.
4. Note per row a size estimate (S/M/L) for promotion, and any ordering dependencies between rows.

## Deliverable

NO code PR. Post the refreshed matrix + findings as ONE structured comment on **#2657** (cross-link from this card), then close this card with a pointer. The maintainer's appetite ruling happens on #2657 afterwards.
